1. Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially when recent prices are high — adjust downward bias for high recent history.
2. Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes in recent history — reduce forecast peak values by 5–15% following a spike.
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecasts tend to overshoot downward trends; apply a slight upward correction when price is falling.
4. Forecast lag: model often lags true price movements by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day moving average.
5. Model overreacts to short-term volatility — suppress forecast volatility when recent 5-day standard deviation is low.
6. When true price is below 70, model tends to overpredict — cap forecast at 70–75 if recent 30-day average is below 70.
7. Model underpredicts when true price is above 85 — increase forecast by 2–5% if recent 30-day average exceeds 85.
